                        </ns0:gap>acred Secret,</ns0:hi> a Mystery to many men, but it is the <ns0:hi>Wisdom of God,</ns0:hi> a Doctrine directing the best means to the best end of man.</ns0:note>, <ns0:hi>even</ns0:hi> the hidden <ns0:hi>wisdom,</ns0:hi> 
                  <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Rom. 16.25, 26. Eph. 3.9. Col. 1.26. 2 Tim. 1.9.</ns0:note> which God ordain<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ed before the world, unto our glory <ns0:note n="m" place="bottom">It is <ns0:hi>hid<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />den wisdom,</ns0:hi> it was ordained of God before the world for our glory, the way of salvation for man, which he had from all Eternity ordained and decreed, but it lay hidden in the secret Counsels of God, till the latter Ages of the World, when it pleased God to send forth his Son into the World to publish it, and after him to appoint us to be the Preachers and Publishers of it.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="8">8 <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Matt. 11.25. Acts. 13.27.</ns0:note> Which none of the Princes of this world knew <ns0:note n="n" place="bottom">Which Divine wisdom neither <ns0:hi>Caiaphas,</ns0:hi> nor <ns0:hi>Pontius Pi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />late,</ns0:hi> nor any considerable number of the Rulers of this Age, whether amongst the Jews, or amongst the Heathens, under<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />stood, though they heard of it.</ns0:note>: for <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Acts. 3.17. See Joh. 16.3.</ns0:note> had they known <ns0:hi>it,</ns0:hi> they would not have crucified the Lord of glory <ns0:note n="o" place="bottom">For if they had so known it, as to have believed, and been perswaded of it, they would never have nailed to the Cross that person, who was the Head and Fountain of it, and the Lord of Glory; both with respect to his Divine Nature, as to which he was <ns0:hi>God blessed for ever,</ns0:hi> and also as <ns0:hi>Mediator,</ns0:hi> being the Author of Glory of those who believe. Nor would this ignorance at all excuse their crucify<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing of Christ, because it was not invincible, they had means sufficient by which they might have come to the knowledge of him, and have understood what he was, so as their ignorance was affected and voluntary.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="9">
                  <ns0:pb facs="tcp:64193:437" />9 But as it is written, Eye hath not seen, nor ear heard, neither have entred into the heart of man, the things which God hath prepared for them that love him <ns0:note n="p" place="bottom">The place where this is written is by all agreed to be <ns0:hi>Isa.</ns0:hi> 64.4. where the words are, <ns0:hi>For since the beginning of the world men have not heard, nor perceived by the ear, neither hath the eye seen, O God, besides thee, what he hath prepared for him that wait<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />eth for him.</ns0:hi> It is so usual with the Penmen of holy Writ, to quote the sense of Texts in the Old Testament, not tying them<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />selves to letters and syllables, that it is mightily vain for any to object against this quotation, as no where written in the Old Testament, but taken out of some <ns0:hi>Apocryphal Writings</ns0:hi> the sense of what is written. <ns0:hi>Isa.</ns0:hi> 64.4. is plainly the same with what he speakeht in this place, the greatest difference is, the Apostle saith, <ns0:hi>Those that love him,</ns0:hi> the Prophet, <ns0:hi>Those that wait for him</ns0:hi> (which is the certain product and effect of love.) The whole 64. Chap. of <ns0:hi>Isaiah,</ns0:hi> and some Chapters following treat concer<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ning Christ, so doth this Text. <ns0:hi>Christ and his benefits</ns0:hi> are to be understood here, by the <ns0:hi>things that God hath prepared for them that love him:</ns0:hi> which are set out as things not <ns0:hi>obvious to sense,</ns0:hi> not to be <ns0:hi>comprehended by reason.</ns0:hi> It could never have entred into the heart of men to conceive, that God should give his on<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ly begotten Son out of his-own bosom, to take upon him our nature, and to dye upon the Cross; or, that Christ should so far humble himself, and become obedient unto death.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="10">10 But <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Matt. 13.11. & 16.17. 1 Joh. 2.27.</ns0:note> God hath revealed <ns0:hi>them</ns0:hi> to us by his Spirit: <ns0:note n="q" place="bottom">God by his Spirit hath opened our understanding to un<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />derstand the holy Scriptures, the Types, and Prophecies of Christ, and what the holy Prophets have spoken of him both as to his Person and Offices.</ns0:note> for the Spirit searcheth all things, yea the deep things of God <ns0:note n="r" place="bottom">For the holy Spirit being the third Person in the blessed Trinity, and so equal with the Fa<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ther and the Son, searcheth the deep things of God, and so is able to reveal to us all the Counsels of God, whatsoever God would have men to understand concerning the Lord Jesus Christ. So as this Text is an evident proof of the Diety of the holy Spirit, he searching the deep things of God, and being alone able to reveal them unto men, so as they shall acknow<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ledge, comprehend, and believe them.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="11">11 For what man knoweth the things of a man, <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Prov. 20.27, & 27.19. Jer. 17.9.</ns0:note> save the spirit of a man that is in him? <ns0:note n="s" place="bottom">Look as it is with a man, No man knoweth his secret thoughts, and counsels, and meanings, save only his own soul that is within him.</ns0:note> even so the things of God knoweth no man, but the Spi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />rit of God <ns0:note n="t" place="bottom">So it is as to the things of God, until God by his Spirit hath revealed them to men, none knoweth them but the holy Spirit of God. It is true as it is with man: when he hath by his tongue discovered his mind to others, they know it so far as he hath so delivered it; but there is no man that discovereth all his thoughts and counsels: so God having in his Word revealed his Will, so far as he hath plainly revealed it, men may know it; but there are deep things of God, My<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />steries in Scripture, which till the Spirit of God hath revealed to men, they know not nor understand; for none knoweth them originally, but the Spirit of God, who is himself God, and <ns0:hi>searcheth the deep things of God.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="12">12 Now we have received, not the spirit of the world <ns0:note n="u" place="bottom">By the spirit of the world some understand the Devil, that evil Spirit which is in the world, and ruleth those that are worldly, carnal men: others understand a meer humane spirit, by which men understand and comprehend meer worldly things. The sense certainly is, we have not a meer worldly instruction and tutouring, we are not taught and instructed from the world (so the Spirit is put for the effects of the Spirit of the world.)</ns0:note>, but <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Rom. 8.15.</ns0:note> the Spirit which is of God, that we might know the things that are freely given to us of God <ns0:note n="w" place="bottom">But we are taught and instructed by the holy Spi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />rit, by which we are taught, and know the things that are free<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ly given us of God, whether they be Divine Mysteries, or Di<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />vine benefits, both what God hath done for us, and what God hath wrought in us.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="13">13 <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">2 Pet. 1.16. See Chap. 1.17.</ns0:note> Which things also we speak, not in the words which mans wisdom teacheth, but which the Holy Ghost teacheth <ns0:note n="x" place="bottom">Reason and all practice directeth men to speak and write of subjects in a stile and phrase fitted to the matter about which they write or discourse. Our subjects, saith the Apostle, were sublime spiritual subjects; therefore I did not discourse them like an Orator, with <ns0:hi>an excellency of speech</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>wisdom</ns0:hi> (as <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 1.) or with the inticing or <ns0:hi>perswasive words of mens wisdom,</ns0:hi> as he had said <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 4. nor with words which <ns0:hi>mans wisdom teacheth</ns0:hi> (which is his phrase here) but with words which the Holy Ghost hath taught us, either in holy Writ, or by its impressions upon our minds, where they are first formed.</ns0:note>, comparing spiritual things with spiritual <ns0:note n="y" place="bottom">Fitting spiritual things to spiri<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tual persons who are able to understand them, or fitting a spi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ritual language to spiritual matter, speaking the Oracles of God as the Oracles of God, 1 <ns0:hi>Pet.</ns0:hi> 4.11. not declaiming like an Orator, nor arguing <ns0:hi>philosophically</ns0:hi> like an <ns0:hi>Athenian Philosopher,</ns0:hi> but using a familiar, plain, spiritual stile, giving you the naked Truths of God without any paint or gawdry of Phrase.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>

Some think that by the <ns0:hi>natural man</ns0:hi> here is meant the <ns0:hi>carnal man:</ns0:hi> thus 1 <ns0:hi>Cor.</ns0:hi> 15.44. the <ns0:hi>na<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tural body</ns0:hi> is opposed to the <ns0:hi>spiritual body</ns0:hi>; besides, they say, that in the constant Phrase of holy Writ, man who is made up of flesh and spirit, as his essential parts, hath constantly his de<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nomination from one of them, and all men in the world are either carnal or spiritual, and that the Greek word <ns0:gap reason="foreign">
                        <ns0:desc>〈 in non-Latin alphabet 〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> signi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />fies that soul and life which is common to all men, from whence all common motions and affections are, and is opposed to the holy Spirit, which dwells in the souls of them that are sanctified, by which they are led and guided, <ns0:hi>&c.</ns0:hi> Thus, say they, the natural man is one who is a servant to his lusts and corruption, under the perfect government of his Soul, considered meerly as natural, all whose motions in that estate of sin and corruption are inordinate. Others think that the Apostle here speaks of such as are weak in the Faith, little ones, Babes in Christ, who had need of milk, not of strong meat, and are natural men in comparison of those more spiritual and perfect. In this sense indeed the Apostle, <ns0:hi>Chap.</ns0:hi> 3. <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 4. calleth them carnal. But there is nothing more plain, than that the Apostle under the notion of <ns0:gap reason="foreign">
                        <ns0:desc>〈 in non-Latin alphabet 〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> (which we translate <ns0:hi>natural man</ns0:hi>) here, understands all such as were not <ns0:hi>perfect</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>spiritual,</ns0:hi> such to whom God had not by his Spirit <ns0:hi>revealed the deep things of God, v.</ns0:hi> 10. such as had only received the <ns0:hi>spirit of the world,</ns0:hi> not the <ns0:hi>Spirit of God,</ns0:hi> by which alone men come to <ns0:hi>know the things</ns0:hi> that are freely given them of God, as <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 12. All these, though some of them are much better than others, having their minds more cultivated and adorned with worldly knowledge and wisdom, yet do not in their hearts (though they may with their ears) receive, that is, believe, embrace, and close with or approve of spiritual and Divine Mysteries, such Doctrines as are purely matters of Faith, standing upon a Divine Revelations.</ns0:note> receiveth not the things of the Spirit of God <ns0:hi>a,</ns0:hi> for they are foolish<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ness unto him <ns0:note n="b" place="bottom">For men of wit and reason count them all foolishness, being neither demonstrable by sense or natural reason.</ns0:note>: <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Rom. 8.7.</ns0:note> neither can he know <ns0:hi>them,</ns0:hi> be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cause they are spiritually discerned <ns0:note n="c" place="bottom">Niether can any man, no otherwise taught and instructed, so compre<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />hend them, as to give a firm and fixed assent to them, or in heart approve them, because they are only to be seen and discerned in a spiritual light, the holy Spirit of God, <ns0:hi>which is the Spirit</ns0:hi> of <ns0:hi>wisdom</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>revelation</ns0:hi> in <ns0:hi>the knowledge of Christ.</ns0:hi> Eph. 1.17, 18. <ns0:hi>In lightning their understandings, that they may know the hope of his calling, and what is the riches of the glory of his inheritance in the Saints, and what is the exceeding greatness of his power to</ns0:hi> them <ns0:hi>that believe, according to the working of his mighty power,</ns0:hi> &c.
